entry.author: Climate Change Commission
entry.summary:
In this webinar, we explore the Commission's first-ever monitoring report on the progress Aotearoa New Zealand is making to adapt to the impacts of climate change. The report looks at the Government's first national adaptation plan (released in 2022), providing an evidence-based, impartial assessment of how effective the plan is and how well it is being implemented.

The full report is available on our website: https://www.climatecommission.govt.nz/nappa-2024

00:00 Introduction – Hikurangi Mills, Principal Analyst
01:50 Overview – Dr Rod Carr, Chair
05:30 Our approach and findings – Jo Hendy, Chief Executive
08:16 Our recommendations
Q&A
14:22 How does this work relate to the current parliamentary inquiry on climate adaptation?
15:39 Taking a more proactive approach to climate impacts
17:23 The Commission's work on mitigation to adaptation
20:40 Legislative tools councils can use for adaptation
23:16 Incentivising adaptation at a local government level
25:30 Community work in South Dunedin and the role for local government
27:49 Intensification and long-term adaptation for flood and coastal areas
29:46 Barriers and obstacles to the scale and pace of adaptation
32:24 Metrics for assessing progress on adaptation
34:05 Grappling with how to do this
36:46 Emergency responses and long term planning
41:40 The role for the insurance industry
43:38 Iwi/Māori, hapū and rūnanga
45:48 What specific and measurable outcomes should be for adaptation
49:58 How the government's plans and policies impact the NAP'S chances of success
51:16 Financial markets leading managed retreat
53:01 Adaptation capabilities and workforce strategy
54:17 Final reflections
